narrative.text: Nucor Corporation engages in the manufacture and sale of steel and steel products. The company operates in three segments: Steel Mills, Steel Products, and Raw Materials. The Steel Mills segment produces hot-rolled, cold-rolled, and galvanized sheet steel products; plate steel products; wide-flange beams, beam blanks, and H-piling and sheet piling structural steel products; and bar steel products, such as blooms, billets, concrete reinforcing and merchant bars, and engineered special bar quality products. This segment sells its products to steel service centers, fabricators, and manufacturers in the United States, Canada, and Mexico, as well as engages in the steel trading and rebar distribution businesses. The Steel Products segment offers steel joists and joist girders, steel decks, and galvanized torque tubes for use in solar arrays, hollow structural section steel tubing, electrical conduit, fabricated concrete reinforcing steel, cold finished steel, steel fasteners, steel grating and expanded metal, wire and wire mesh, metal building systems, insulated metal panels, steel racking, overhead doors, and utility towers and structures for communications and energy transmission. This segment is also involved in the piling distribution business. The Raw Materials segment produces direct reduced iron (DRI); brokers ferrous and nonferrous metals, pig iron, hot briquetted iron, and DRI; supplies ferro-alloys; processes ferrous and nonferrous scrap metal; and engages in the natural gas production and industrial gas business. This segment sells its ferrous scrap to electric arc furnace steel mills and foundries for manufacturing process; and nonferrous scrap metal to aluminum can producers, secondary aluminum smelters, steel mills and other processors, and consumers of various nonferrous metals. Nucor Corporation was founded in 1905 and is based in Charlotte, North Carolina.

base.writtenAnchor: Nucor grows revenue around 4% a year, between the 6.1% eight-year window CAGR and the flat-to-down pricing of the past two fiscal years, helped by the volume recovery visible in the July 2026 quarter (+23% year on year, trailing twelve months 36.1bn against 32.5bn of FY2025 revenue). The operating margin settles near the median of the FY2017-FY2025 cash proxy (operating cash flow less D&A over revenue, roughly 10%), i.e. mid-cycle rather than peak or trough. Net reinvestment runs above the 3.7% historic median as the recent mill programme is completed but below the 6.8% of FY2025, and new capital earns about the discount rate, which is what an undifferentiated-but-efficient commodity producer should earn over a cycle.

bear.writtenAnchor: Steel prices and volumes mean-revert after the 2021-2022 spike. Revenue drifts down about 2% a year from the 2025 base as imports and new domestic capacity press on pricing, and the cash margin proxy stays near the weak end of the filed decade (FY2017 and FY2025 levels). The large capital programme of FY2024-FY2025 keeps depreciation rising while contributing little incremental profit, so the return on new dollars sits below the 11% discount rate and stock compensation slowly lifts the share count. This is a case where the last five years of spending bought capacity into a softer market.

bull.writtenAnchor: The new sheet, plate and downstream capacity funded by the 2.2bn-3.4bn annual capex of FY2023-FY2025 ramps into firm demand. Revenue compounds about 8% a year, in line with the 23% year-on-year growth in the latest quarter persisting into mid-cycle volumes, and the margin runs near the upper half of the filed cash-flow record (FY2021 and FY2023 proxies of 15-18%) without reaching the 2022 peak. New investment earns around 13%, above the 12.5% bull terminal hurdle, so growth adds value; the share count is held flat.
